title: CmdPal: One hung extension blocks the entire stop loop (EXT26.T2)

judgment.rationale: Source inspection identifies a sequential synchronous COM path and no service-level deadline. The report explicitly says a hung extension was not tested, so a controlled maintainer test is the next step.
judgment.recommended_action: Use the targeted maintainer reproduction to validate the proposed mechanism before design approval; no upstream action has been taken.
evidence: SignalStopAsync checks liveness and disposes extensions sequentially; its per-extension catch handles throws, not hangs.
The restart path's five-second caller wait does not bound the service loop or ordinary reload.
The issue states no extension was deliberately hung.

fix_assessment.rationale: No matching fix was identified by focused issue-number search; keep the mechanism as a hypothesis pending reproduction.

plan: Reproduce with controllably blocked IsRunning and Dispose calls and measure the service wait.
Bound the wait without treating timeout as COM cancellation; retain ownership and cap in-flight calls across repeated stops.
Attempt other providers despite one blocked call and prevent late completion from clearing replacements.
Add timeout, repeated-stop, late-completion and healthy-peer tests.
verification: Block the first provider's IsRunning and Dispose calls separately; verify a healthy second provider is still signaled.
Repeat stop while blocked and confirm ownership stays bounded.
Release after registering a replacement and verify the late call cannot affect it.

proposed_fixes.root_cause: Synchronous COM liveness/disposal calls run serially without a service-level deadline or bounded ownership; one hang can prevent later extensions from being signaled.

confidence.rationale: The sequential synchronous path is source-confirmed, but no hang was reproduced; timeouts cannot cancel COM and require explicit ownership tests.

steps: 1. Start two extensions and block the first IsRunning or Dispose call.
